outcome: Innate and adaptive immune cell phenotype (B-cell subset homeostasis)
Vaccine-induced antibody responses (anti-Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) and anti-tetanus toxoid immunoglobulin G titers)
Susceptibility to encapsulated bacterial disease and pneumonia
cohort: The study participants were Human immunodeficiency virus-exposed uninfected (HEU) and HIV-unexposed uninfected (HU) infants born to HIV-infected or HIV-uninfected pregnant women.
finding: HIV exposure in infants may dysregulate monocyte and B-cell function, leading to lower vaccine-induced anti-Haemophilus influenzae type b and anti-tetanus toxoid immunoglobulin G titers during immune maturation, which could contribute to increased bacterial disease risk.
